Criminal Investigation Department,
Second Division.

Shanghai,
February 26, 1929.

Inspector Bardy to the Chief of the Criminal Investigation
Department.

I have the honour to report that at about 2 a.m.
February 25/4 a fire broke out in the No. 2 Lane 146/A
Route des Soeurs. The Fire Brigade was informed at 2:34
a.m. and quickly proceeded to the place where they found
flames emerging from several windows of rooms on the
second story of the house, west corner. After making
the customary dispositions, the firemen made use of a
ladder and gained access to the place on fire, it having
been reported that a child was there. Mr. Boyere placed
a handkerchief in his mouth and without hesitation entered
the place. He succeeded in approaching a bed which was
in flames and by groping he ascertained that a body was
lying on it. He carefully took it into his arms and
carried it through the flames to an adjoining verandah.
Following upon an inquiry, it was established that the
person who had been taken from the burning room was Mrs.
Clausing, wife of an American officer of the Army of
Occupation of Shanghai and who was living at the address
given above.
After 2 hours of work, the firemen, under the
direction of their chief Mr. Chapeaux, overcame the flames.
The damage done is rather serious and is not covered by
insurance. The premises were used as a boardinghouse
by Mr. Poliak. The causes of the fire have not been
entirely ascertained and appeared to have been accidental.
The inquiry has not revealed anything definite.
The body of Mrs. Clausing was removed to the Mortuary
of the Municipal Hospital where Dr. Velliet made medical-
legal examination. He has issued a certificate for
burial which he has personally handed to Lieutenant Evans
Fordyce Carlson who attended the examination with the
Police. In the evening the body was removed to the
Pearson Road Mortuary, International Settlement.
The causes of the fire could not be definitely
ascertained during the preliminary investigation. The
French Police, who have no complaint whatever, were not
in a position to interrogate the person responsible for
the accident. As he is an American officer an inquiry
has been opened by a Judge of the American Court.

Sgd:- BARDY.

刑事调查处，
第二科。

上海，
1929年2月26日。

巴迪巡长致刑事调查处处长。

谨此报告，2月25/4日凌晨2时许，修女路（Route des Soeurs）146/A弄2号发生火灾。消防队于凌晨2:34接到通知并迅速赶赴现场，发现该房屋西角二楼的几个房间窗户冒出火焰。在采取常规措施后，消防员使用梯子进入着火区域，因为据报有一名儿童在那里。博耶尔（Boyere）先生将手帕塞入口中，毫不犹豫地进入屋内。他成功接近一张正在燃烧的床，并通过摸索确定床上躺着一具尸体。他小心地将其抱起，穿过火焰带到相邻的阳台上。经查询，确认从燃烧房间救出的人是克劳辛（Clausing）夫人，她是驻沪美军占领军的一名美国军官的妻子，居住在上述地址。
经过2小时的扑救，消防员在其队长夏波（Chapeaux）先生的指挥下扑灭了大火。损失相当严重，且未投保。该场所由波利亚克（Poliak）先生用作寄宿公寓。火灾原因尚未完全查明，似乎是意外事故。调查未发现任何确切线索。
克劳辛夫人的遗体被送往市立医院停尸房，由韦利埃（Velliet）医生进行法医检验。他签发了埋葬许可证，并亲自交给埃文斯·福特伊斯·卡尔森（Evans Fordyce Carlson）中尉，后者会同警方参加了检验。当晚，遗体被移至公共租界皮尔逊路（Pearson Road）停尸房。
在初步调查期间，无法明确确定火灾原因。法租界警方因未收到任何投诉，无权讯问事故责任人。由于他是美国军官，美国法院法官已立案调查。

签名：- 巴迪（BARDY）。

SERVICE DE LA SURETE
------
2ème. Division

Shanghai, le 26 Février 1929

L'Inspecteur BARDY
à monsieur le Chef de la Sûreté,

J'ai l'honneur de vous rendre compte que dans la nuit
du 23 au 24 Février, vers 2 heures du matin, un incendie a
éclaté au N° 2 Passage 146 A.Route des Soeurs. Les pompiers
alertés à 2 h.24, se sont rapidement rendus sur les lieux et
ont constaté que des flammes jaillissaient de plusieurs fe-
nêtres des pièces situées au deuxième étage de la maison et
sises à l'angle Ouest. Après avoir pris les dispositions
d'usage, les pompiers ont appliqué une échelle et ont pu
avoir accès au lieu incendié, un enfant y ayant été signalé.
Mr. KUYERE a mis un mouchoir sur sa bouche et sans hésitati-
on y a pénétré. Il a réussi à s'approcher du lit qui brûlait
et, à tâtons, a pu se rendre compte qu'un cadavre y gisait.
Précautionneusement il l'a pris dans ses bras et au milieu
des flammes a pu le transporter sur une véranda attenante.
Par la suite et l'enquête, il fut établi que la personne qui
avait été retirée de la chambre incendiée était Mme CLAUSING,
femme d'un Officier Américain, du Corps d'Occupation de
Shanghai et résidant actuellement à l'adresse précitée.
Après 2 heures d'efforts, les pompiers, dirigés par
Mr. le Commandant CHAPEAUX, purent maîtriser le sinistre.
Les dégâts sont assez élevés et ne sont couverts par
aucune assurance. La maison incendiée est une pension de
famille tenue par Mr. POLIAK.

致保安处处长先生，

谨此报告，2月23日至24日夜间，凌晨2时许，修女路（Route des Soeurs）146 A弄2号发生火灾。消防员于2时24分接到警报，迅速赶赴现场，发现火焰从位于房屋西角的二楼几个房间的窗户喷出。在采取常规措施后，消防员架设梯子，得以进入着火地点，因为据报有一名儿童在那里。库耶尔（KUYERE）先生将手帕捂在嘴上，毫不犹豫地进入屋内。他成功接近燃烧的床铺，并通过摸索发现有一具尸体躺在上面。他小心翼翼地将其抱起，在火焰中将其转移到相邻的阳台上。随后经调查确认，从着火房间救出的人是克劳辛（CLAUSING）夫人，她是驻沪美军占领军的一名美国军官的妻子，目前居住在上述地址。
经过2小时的努力，消防员在夏波（CHAPEAUX）指挥官的指挥下控制了灾情。
损失相当高昂，且没有任何保险覆盖。着火的房屋是由波利亚克（POLIAK）先生经营的寄宿公寓。

Les causes de l'incendie n'ont pu être entièrement
définies et paraissent être accidentelles. L'enquête n'a
pas permis de relever quoi que ce soit de précis.

Le corps de Mme CLAUSING a été transporté à la morgue

d'inhumer qu'il a remis lui-même à Mr. le Lieutenant Améri-
cain Evans Fordyce Carlson, qui, avec nous assistait aux
constatations.

Dans la soirée, le corps a été transféré à la morgue
de Fearon Road, au Quartier International.

Les causes du sinistre n'ont pu être définies au cours

étant Officier Américain, l'instruction a été ouverte par un
Juge siégeant à la Cour Américaine./.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 6, 1929.

Verdict Returned By Jury In
Frenchtown Fire Tragedy

A verdict in the case of the mysterious death of Mrs. J. G. Clausing, wife of an American Marine officer, yesterday was returned by a Coroner's jury before Commissioner A. Krisel in the American Court. Death was caused, the jury found, by causes unknown. Thus ends an inquest which for the past week has held the centre of the news stage of Shanghai. Mrs. Clausing was found dead following a fire at 146A Route des Soeurs, a little more than a week ago.

The first red tongue of flame from that fire, shooting up into a night sky and noted by passers-by, marked the beginning of a double tragedy which has stirred the foreign community. Within the burning house Mrs. Clausing was found dead—under circumstances that breathed of mystery. Lieut. Clausing, her husband, was painfully burned. He died a few days later in the Marine Hospital as the result of infection from his burns.

The verdict and findings of the jury read as follow:

"We, the jury, find that the body examined by us at the International Funeral Directors' Parlours at 71 Kiaochow Road at 4.30 p.m. on February 25, to be that of Ruth Lois Clausing, a citizen of the United States of America, and that she came to her death in her apartment at 146A Route des Soeurs between the hours of 11.15 p.m. of February 23, 1929 and 2.50 a.m. of February 24, 1929, through causes unknown. During this time a fire of unknown origin occurred in her apartment from the debris of which her charred remains were later removed."

The coroner then thanked the members of the jury as follows: "Gentlemen of the jury, the coroner fully appreciates the services that you gentlemen have been called upon to make. On being summoned as a jury you promptly laid aside your various businesses and responded to the duty of a jury in investigating the circumstances of this inquest.

"You have very intelligently and thoroughly inquired into this matter. You have given a great deal of your time and attention to it and I am fully convinced that in reaching the verdict you have, that you have done so after a mature deliberation. Your verdict is approved and we desire to thank you very much indeed."

陪审团对法租界火灾悲剧作出裁决

昨天，在美国法院，由专员 A.克里塞尔（A. Krisel）主持的验尸陪审团对美国海军陆战军官 J.G.克劳辛（J. G. Clausing）夫人神秘死亡一案作出了裁决。陪审团认定，死因不明。至此，过去一周占据上海新闻舞台中心的验尸程序宣告结束。克劳辛夫人是一周多前在修女路（Route des Soeurs）146A号火灾后发现死亡的。

那场火灾的第一道红色火舌射向夜空，被路人注意到，标志着一场震惊外籍社群的双重悲剧的开始。在燃烧的房子里，克劳辛夫人被发现死亡——情况充满神秘色彩。她的丈夫克劳辛中尉严重烧伤。几天后，他因烧伤感染在海軍陸戰隊醫院去世。

陪审团的裁决和调查结果如下：

“我们，陪审团，认定我们于2月25日下午4时30分在胶州路71号国际殡仪馆查验的尸体为美国公民露丝·洛伊丝·克劳辛（Ruth Lois Clausing），并认定她于1929年2月23日晚上11时15分至1929年2月24日凌晨2时50分之间，在修女路146A号的公寓内，因不明原因死亡。在此期间，其公寓内发生了一起起因不明的火灾，她的烧焦遗骸后来从废墟中被移出。”

随后，验尸官感谢陪审团成员，致辞如下：“陪审团的先生们，验尸官充分感激各位先生被召来提供服务。在作为陪审员被传唤时，你们立即放下各自的事务，响应履行陪审团职责，调查本次验尸的情况。

“你们非常明智且彻底地调查了此事。你们为此投入了大量的时间和注意力，我完全确信，你们在经过成熟审议后作出了这一裁决。批准你们的裁决，我们要向你们表示非常感谢。”

a. c (Pal)

文森特·奥古斯都·贝克（Vincent Augustus Baker）随后出庭作证，称他住在埃斯特拉公寓（Estella Apartments）的五楼。“事发当天早上，我被妻子叫醒，她告诉我消防队已经到了，她不确定受灾的是不是我们这栋楼。从我们的卧室窗户可以俯瞰救火路（Route des Seours）以及通往涉案两栋建筑的通道，我确实看到了火焰。当我走到楼梯平台时，我看见麦坎德利斯小姐（Miss McCandless），她说她非常懊恼，因为她早在火势初期就发现了火情，并试图打电话，但未能接通电话交换台，她觉得如果她能早点联系上他们，或许就能保住这栋房子。那时，我们并不知道现场有任何人。她没有提到看见游廊上有人。

我没有看见任何人被抬出大楼。我看见消防员试图带着一个从房间里拿出来的包裹爬下梯子；他们没能成功，于是把包裹放在了游廊上。我没有看见任何穿着衬衫和长裤的男人站在大门入口附近，我也从未与任何像麦坎德利斯小姐作证所说的那样看见游廊上有男人的人交谈过。把我妻子吵醒的不是哨声，而是消防队的到来。”

因为当时只有三四夸脱瓶装的啤酒，据我所见，没有饮用其他烈性酒。我曾见过克劳辛夫人（Mrs. Clausing）走到餐具柜旁喝酒，而其他人并没有喝，但在这次场合我没有看见她这样做，尽管她有机会这样做。克劳辛夫妇和我一起离开，我们都去了另一位朋友家，大约6点30分到达那里，当时共有10人聚会。我们在那里喝了马提尼鸡尾酒。我待了大约四分之三小时。和我在一起的那位女士和我大约在7点30分离开。我们每人只喝了两三杯鸡尾酒，在我们离开时，克劳辛先生和夫人都没有醉酒。

“随后我们去了斯诺上尉（Capt. Snow）的住所，就在同一栋房子里，克劳辛夫妇也在那里，一共五人聚会。那大约是7点钟，我在8点30分离开，克劳辛夫妇在我们之后大约十五分钟离开。喝掉的啤酒不超过两夸脱瓶装，克劳辛先生和夫人都喝了一部分。

房间角落里的梳妆台上放着朗姆酒和伏特加。

塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellet）：你有理由相信克劳辛夫人在那时自己拿了酒喝吗？——我没看见她这样做。

在你离开的时候，你认为克劳辛夫人是否醉酒？——那时她能走路，但我说再喝一点就会让她醉酒。我以前见过她喝酒，也见过她醉酒，只需很少的量就能让她醉。我从未见过克劳辛先生和他的妻子激烈争吵或发生严重分歧，也从未听克劳辛夫人说过关于自杀的话，虽然她曾说过她永远不会离开中国。他们的想法不同：我认为她想出去参加聚会，而他不想。我从未见过克劳辛中尉（Lieut. Clausing）喝到事后记不起发生过什么的程度。我从未听说他在那种状态下失忆过。

塞莱特博士：有证据表明，在10点后不久，当他们到家时，克劳辛夫人醉得无法在没有协助的情况下走出汽车，并且需要协助才能上楼回到自己的房间，当她到达那里时醉得如此厉害，以至于她没有坐在椅子上，而是坐在了地板上。你会说在她离开斯诺家时，她就醉成那样了吗？——嗯，我曾和她一起吃过晚饭，并在某个晚上和她打过桥牌，她当时看起来还好，然而她走进浴室，出来后却坐在了地板上。

如果得知假设克劳辛中尉喝的酒不超过你所见他喝的量，而他在12点钟时却严重醉酒，你会感到惊讶吗？——是的。

这位证人以断言结束他的证词，他确信他所看到的尸体是克劳辛夫人的，因为他辨认出了他清晰可见的她口中的两颗金磨牙。

征集证人

验尸官克里尔先生（Mr. Kriel）希望任何目睹火灾并认为自己掌握有价值信息的人，能与他或美国检察官塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellet）联系，地址为黄浦路11号美国法院。诉讼程序随即休庭，直至今天上午10点继续。

路边抢劫

昨晚深夜，五名男子（其中两人蒙面）闯入静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的一处住宅，窃走了大量钱财和财物。据报道暂无逮捕行动。

胸部冒出粉刺

灼热和瘙痒持续不断。库蒂库拉（Cuticura）治愈

“我深受胸前冒出的小粉刺困扰，它们持续的灼热和瘙痒给我带来了极大的痛苦。刺激感加剧，粉刺逐渐扩散到我的背部、颈部和手臂。它们大约有豌豆大小，颜色鲜红。

“我看到了库蒂库拉香皂和软膏的广告，并索取了免费样品。使用后我得到了缓解，因此购买了一盒软膏和一块香皂，随后我便痊愈了。”（签名）E. 汤普森夫人（Mrs. E. Thompson），美国马萨诸塞州波士顿市亨利街6号，8月。

"Last Saturday night at about 10 o'clock I saw Mrs. Clausing. She took her upstairs, helping the body because she was drunk. The master also was drunk, but better than the Missus. He could walk himself. I didn't see the Missus again. I went to sleep and woke up hearing whistles. I looked out of the window and saw red so I went to the back door, and saw there were flames bursting through the windows of Mr. Clausing's rooms. I woke up the cook. I saw the Russian lady who lives on the first floor in the hall. I used to put coal on the fires in Mr Clausing's room. There was coal in the coal receptacle. I didn't see two men carrying out another man or body."

George Pollak testified that Mrs Hacquardt, after he had told her and, showing her a watch, asked if it was hers. She didn't know of the gentleman's name, but she described the watch which he had lost. "I have heard what has been said about two men carrying one another, but I have not the slightest idea as to who it could have been."

MORE ABOUT THE WATCH

Alexander Pollak, sworn, stated that he first heard of Mrs. Hacquard having seen someone with a watch that answered the description of his brother's watch. "I did not pay much attention to it, but afterwards she told me she saw two men carrying out another man. I asked her if she had told the police, and she said: No. I heard Miss Norah Reuter testify yesterday, and her mother, about seeing the American, Lieut. Clausing, while the fire was going on, and I heard on Tuesday about 12 o'clock the same thing from Mrs Hacquardt. I saw one or two policemen whistling, and I heard a lot of noise of people outside, but I heard no noise in the vicinity of Lieut. Clausing's room, and I saw nobody go up to his room. I saw a man fully dressed in a blue suit or a blue sailor's uniform go up to his room. I saw no person at any time; I saw no one around the house anywhere that would answer the description of those three men—one being carried and two carrying him. I cannot account in any way for the story of two men carrying a third man. I heard no sound of a whistle being blown from an elevation.

"TELL US THE TRUTH"

The Coroner: We ask you to tell us all the truth. Is there nothing else that you now remember that you can tell us?—I have told all the truth that I know.

We want to know all that you know about this thing. Have you overlooked telling us something?—There were thieves, or robbers, in house No. 1 because the lock of one of the tenants' rooms was broken. It was broken after he had left the premises, after the fire, but as far as I know nothing was stolen; there was an attempt to break a door in the attic of No. 1 house, but so far as I know there was nothing stolen in house No. 2.

Are you sure that when you were up in your cousin's room at about 11.30 you didn't hear any noises whatever in the Clausing's rooms?

You heard that Miss Reuter and her mother testified that they heard noises in the direction of Clausing's room—I heard that, but I didn't hear any such noises at any time that night.

Miss Norah Reuter, who gave such important evidence yesterday, was re-called for further questioning, and, in answer to the District Attorney, stated that when she first saw Lieut. Clausing, while the fire was going on, the brigade had already arrived.

Where was Clausing when you first saw him?—Near the entrance gate; he had his hands in his pockets, and he did not take them out of his pockets; I saw his burnt arms, and I do not recall his singlet as being stained or dirtied. It was not even burnt; it was a white sleeveless one.

ADVICE TO CLAUSING

What conversation did you have with him?—I came up to him, and I said: Are you the American man from upstairs? He said: Yes. I said: Where is your wife? He said: She is out. I said: What are you doing here you are all burnt up; you ought to go and see a doctor at the hospital. He said: Alright, I will go, and he then left me.

You didn't ask him any other questions?—No, nothing else.

Are you sure you saw him after

torso, a singlet which had been taken from Lt. Clausing's body and which was alleged to have been worn when the fire occurred.

Assumed that a man had those burns in the places and manner you have described, could he had been wearing this singlet, do you think? "No, if he had had this singlet on it would have shown signs of the burning."

Then you would think that he put the singlet on after he had sustained the burns? Yes.

Look at the back of the singlet, about the place where the shoulder blade would be. What do you think of this stain there? Possibly it is the exudation from burns, but there is a case of what looks like skin attached to it. It is my opinion that Lt. Clausing could not have had this singlet on at the time he sustained those burns.

EXTRAORDINARY SILENCE

At the first meeting when Lt. Clausing told you he was all right, did he say anything to you as to how he received his injuries? —None. There was also no conversation whatsoever at the second meeting and on all the subsequent days that I saw him he never mentioned his injuries to me and never discussed with him his injuries nor had any conversation with him at all.

The Coroner: Didn't you hear anybody talk to him about his injuries? I heard an officer talk to him while I was there, and I understood him to say that he didn't know why Mrs. Clausing had gone back into the room. I didn't hear him say to the officer that he knew Mrs. Clausing had gone back to his room. I am not sure who the officer was. Part of the top surface, extending to the back of the head, was singed, and his head would not have been so singed had he been lying on his back on a pillow, and if he had been lying on his side it would leave a portion of his hair, on that side, unsinged, but I noticed that his whole head was singed. The fingers of the right hand looked as if they had been bleeding. The burn in the left palm might have been caused by getting hold of a hot door-knob or if he had got hold of an iron rod. I understand from him that the burn in the hand was due to trying to open something either a trunk or a locker.

SOME SUPPOSITIONS

Dr. Seibert: Suppose a man were lying in bed asleep and the bed caught fire—such a fire as would be caused by a match or a cigarette—no gasoline or anything like that—do you think it possible that a man in normal condition would not be awakened until he was burnt to the extent that you discovered Lt. Clausing was burnt? I think he would have been aroused very much earlier.

Suppose Lt. Clausing had had a great deal to drink; that he had his last drink not later than 9.45 p.m., and that he went to bed a few hours later—and was aroused by the fire about 2.15, or 2.30 a.m. —almost five hours later—do you think a man might still be so much under the influence of the liquor that he had taken five hours before, that he would be numb to the extent that he would not be aroused by these flames, as surely as you would expect him to be?—I don't think so; I think the only way it could probably happen is that he should have been in such a state of intoxication as to have produced coma.

Suppose a man like Lt. Clausing had a large quantity of liquor before 9 and 9.45, and he remained awake until, say, 11.30, and then

went to bed without anything to drink in that intervening time, do you think it at all possible that coma would be induced after the lapse of that period?—It is possible, but very improbable; coma usually follows close upon the consumption of liquor.

And not two or three hours later? —It might take one or two hours; it all depends upon the person.

Supposing a woman had had a considerable quantity to drink, so that she was very much intoxicated, and unable to control her movements, and after a period of two or three hours she went to bed and then was subjected to this ordeal by fire; do you think it possible that she might be burnt to death without even being aware that there was fire?—I think it might be possible.

Even though she was awake until at least as late as 11.30?—I think it is possible that she was asleep, and in such a state that the flames in the room might overcome her.

Could a man rush through a burning room with the room all in flames, and only have his hair singed?—I don't think so; it all depends how fast he went through the room.

ANOTHER WITNESS

Miss Edith J. C. McCandless, who, sworn, stated that she was Irish then gave evidence to the effect that she was employed in the Hampton & Shanghai Banking Corporation. "On Saturday I was out at the Majestic and reached my room in the Estrella Apartments, on the corner of Route des Sports and Avenue Joffre at 1.15 a.m. I live on the 5th floor, and after 12 o'clock we have to walk up. I was passing my key in the hole, when I saw smoke from a house in the Court just below a sheet of flame."

MAN ON THE VERANDAH

"I stood there looking, and soon afterwards I saw a man on the verandah in his pyjamas. He was whistling; he was not shouting. He was trying to get over the rails, which he succeeded in doing, but he was not able to get down. The window happened to be open, and I shouted out to him to wait a minute, run down the stairs, and get a lot of Chinese in the street, whom I told to go to the house and help. Then I ran upstairs again, opened my door and tried to telephone. All this time the man was still whistling. As soon as I got to my room, I went to the telephone, but I was an awfully long time in getting connected. Eventually I got on to the French Police station, and told them there was a fire near my apartments but I could not say where, but that they could soon find out. The man said he smothered, and in five minutes thereafter the fire brigade arrived. In the meantime, the man had disappeared, and was not on the balcony any longer; I don't know how he got away.

WOMAN'S SCREAMS

"I heard a woman scream two or three times, but whether from downstairs or not I couldn't say.

When I first saw the man on the balcony I don't know there were no flames in the building at all, and the man must evidently have felt that he was trapped. The woman's screams I heard seemed to come from the window of the room where the flames were. One of the screams was loud and two rather faint. They were screams of someone thoroughly frightened."

"I was on my verandah looking out, and saw all that I have related; I could feel the heat, and during all the time that I stayed —about three minutes—the man was on the verandah. He was well built, of average height, and, I should judge, young. I saw everything very clearly. I did not see any body carried out through the Court-yard. 致命火灾事件
由证人回顾

（续自第1页，第4栏。）

睡觉。这取决于他的职责是保持克劳辛中尉（Lieut. Clausing）及其妻子所居住的房间清洁。

“上周六晚上大约10点钟，我看见了克劳辛太太。我把她扶上楼，搀扶着她的身体，因为她喝醉了。主人也喝醉了，但比女主人情况好些。他能自己走路。我没再看见女主人。我去睡觉了，听到哨声后醒来。我向窗外看，看到红光，所以我走到后门，看见克劳辛先生房间的窗户里喷出火焰。我叫醒了厨师。我看见住在二楼大厅的那位俄罗斯女士。我过去常往克劳辛先生房间的炉子里加煤。煤斗里有煤。我没看见两个人抬着另一个人或一具尸体。”

乔治·波拉克（George Pollak）作证说，哈夸特太太（Mrs Hacquardt）在他告诉她并给她看一块手表，问她是否是她的时候……她不知道那位绅士的名字，但她描述了他丢失的手表。“我听说过关于两个人抬着一个人的说法，但我完全不知道那会是谁。”

关于手表的更多情况

亚历山大·波拉克（Alexander Pollak），经宣誓，陈述说他最初听说哈夸德太太（Mrs. Hacquard）看见某人带着一块符合他弟弟手表特征的手表。“我当时没太注意，但后来她告诉我，她看见两个人抬着另一个人出去。我问她是否告诉了警察，她说：没有。我昨天听见诺拉·罗伊特小姐（Miss Norah Reuter）和她母亲作证，说在火灾进行时看见了美国人克劳辛中尉，我在星期二大约12点从哈夸特太太那里听到了同样的事情。我看见一两名警察在吹哨子，我听见外面有很多人嘈杂的声音，但我没听见克劳辛中尉房间附近有任何声音，也没看见有人上他的房间。我看见一个穿着全套蓝色西装或蓝色水手制服的人走上他的房间。我任何时候都没看见任何人；我在房子周围任何地方都没看见符合那三个人描述的人——一人被抬，两人抬着他。我无法以任何方式解释关于两个人抬着第三个人的故事。我没听见从高处传来吹哨子的声音。

“告诉我们真相”

验尸官：我们要求你告诉我们全部真相。你现在还记得有什么其他事情可以告诉我们吗？——我已经告诉了我所知道的全部真相。

我们想知道你对这件事所知的一切。你是否遗漏了告诉我们要说的某些事情？——1号房里有小偷或强盗，因为其中一间租户房间的锁被破坏了。那是他离开寓所后，即火灾之后被破坏的，但据我所知没有东西被盗；有人试图撬开1号房屋阁楼的门，但据我所知，2号房屋里没有东西被盗。

你确定当你在大约11点30分在你表弟的房间里时，你没有听见克劳辛房间里有任何声音吗？

你听见罗伊特小姐和她母亲作证说她们听见克劳辛房间方向有声音——我听见了，但那天晚上任何时间我都没听见这样的声音。

昨天提供了重要证词的诺拉·罗伊特小姐被重新传唤接受进一步询问，并在回答地区检察官提问时陈述说，当她第一次看见克劳辛中尉时，火灾正在进行，消防队已经到达。

当你第一次看见克劳辛时，他在哪里？——在大门入口附近；他双手插在口袋里，没有把手拿出来；我看见他被烧伤的手臂，我不记得他的背心有污渍或弄脏。甚至没有烧焦；那是一件白色的无袖背心。

给克劳辛的建议

你和他进行了什么谈话？——我走到他跟前，说：你是楼上的那个美国人吗？他说：是的。我说：你妻子在哪里？他说：她出去了。我说：你全身都烧伤了，在这里做什么；你应该去医院看医生。他说：好的，我去，然后他就离开了我。

你没问他其他问题吗？——没有，没问别的。

你确定你在……之后看见了他

躯干，一件从克劳辛中尉尸体上取下的背心，据称火灾发生时他穿着这件背心。

假设一个人像你描述的那样，在这些部位以这种方式遭受烧伤，你认为他当时可能穿着这件背心吗？“不，如果他穿着这件背心，上面会有烧伤的痕迹。”

那么你会认为他是在遭受烧伤后才穿上这件背心的吗？是的。

看看背心的背面，大约在肩胛骨的位置。你觉得那里的污渍是什么？可能是烧伤渗出的液体，但上面附着一块看起来像皮肤的东西。我认为克劳辛中尉在遭受那些烧伤时不可能穿着这件背心。

异常的沉默

在第一次见面时，当克劳辛中尉告诉你他没事时，他有没有跟你说他是如何受伤的？——没有。第二次见面时也没有任何交谈，在此后我看到他的所有日子里，他从未向我提及他的伤势，我也从未与他讨论过他的伤势，根本没有与他进行过任何交谈。

验尸官：你没听见有人跟他谈论他的伤势吗？我在那里时听见一名警官跟他说话，我理解他说他不知道克劳辛太太为什么回到房间里。我没听见他对警官说他知道克劳辛太太回到了他的房间。我不确定那名警官是谁。头顶部分表面延伸至后脑勺的部分被烧焦，如果他是仰面躺在枕头上，他的头不会烧焦成那样；如果他是侧卧，那一侧的头发会有一部分未烧焦，但我注意到他的整个头部都被烧焦了。右手的手指看起来像是在流血。左手掌的烧伤可能是由于抓住热的门把手，或者抓住了铁杆造成的。我从他那里了解到，手部的烧伤是由于试图打开某样东西，无论是箱子还是储物柜。

一些推测

塞伯特医生（Dr. Seibert）：假设一个人正躺在床上睡觉，床着火了——这种火是由火柴或香烟引起的——没有汽油或类似的东西——你认为一个处于正常状态的人有可能直到烧到你发现克劳辛中尉那种程度才会醒来吗？我认为他很早就会被惊醒。

假设克劳辛中尉喝了很多酒；他最后一次喝酒不晚于晚上9点45分，几小时后上床睡觉——大约在凌晨2点15分或2点30分被火灾惊醒——差不多五个小时后——你认为一个人可能仍然受到五小时前摄入的酒精的影响，以至于他对这些火焰麻木，不像你期望的那样被惊醒吗？——我不这么认为；我认为唯一可能发生的情况是他处于一种导致昏迷的醉酒状态。

假设像克劳辛中尉这样的人在9点到9点45分之前喝了大量酒，他一直醒着，比如到11点30分，然后

在那段间隔时间里没再喝酒就去睡觉了，你认为在那段时间过后有可能引发昏迷吗？——有可能，但非常不可能；昏迷通常紧随饮酒之后发生。

而不是两三个小时后？——可能需要一两个小时；这完全取决于个人。

假设一个女人喝了不少酒，以至于醉得很厉害，无法控制自己的行动，过了两三个小时后她上床睡觉，然后遭受了这场火灾的折磨；你认为她有可能在甚至没有意识到有火灾的情况下被烧死吗？——我认为这可能。

即使她一直醒着直到至少11点30分？——我认为她有可能睡着了，并且处于一种房间里的火焰可能制服她的状态。

一个人能冲过一个满是火焰的房间，而只有头发被烧焦吗？——我不这么认为；这完全取决于他穿过房间的速度。

另一位证人

伊迪丝·J·C·麦坎德利斯小姐（Miss Edith J. C. McCandless），经宣誓，陈述她是爱尔兰人，随后提供的证词大意是她在汇丰银行（Hampton & Shanghai Banking Corporation，注：此处原文可能有误，通常指HSBC，但按原文直译为汉普顿与上海银行公司，或为笔误）工作。“周六我在美琪大戏院（Majestic）外出，凌晨1点15分回到位于体育路（Route des Sports）和霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）拐角处的埃斯特雷拉公寓（Estrella Apartments）的房间。我住在5楼，12点后我们必须走楼梯上去。当我把钥匙插进锁孔时，我看见下面院子里的一所房子里冒烟，紧接着是一片火焰。”

阳台上的男人

“我站在那里看着，不久后我看见一个穿着睡衣的男人在阳台上。他在吹口哨；他没有喊叫。他试图翻过栏杆，他成功做到了，但他下不去。窗户正好开着，我向他大喊，让他等一下，跑下楼梯，找街上的许多中国人，我让他们去那所房子帮忙。然后我又跑上楼，打开门，试图打电话。在这段时间里，那个人一直在吹口哨。我一回到房间，就去打电话，但花了很长时间才接通。最终我联系上了法国警察局，告诉他们我的公寓附近发生了火灾，但我说不清具体位置，不过他们很快就能查到。那人说他窒息了，五分钟后消防队就到了。与此同时，那个人消失了，不在阳台上了；我不知道他是怎么离开的。

女人的尖叫声

“我听见一个女人尖叫了两三次，但我不确定是不是从楼下传来的。

当我第一次看见阳台上的男人时，我不知道建筑物里根本没有火焰，那个人显然一定觉得自己被困住了。我听见的女人的尖叫声似乎来自有火焰的房间窗户。其中一声尖叫很大声，另外两声比较微弱。那是极度恐惧的人发出的尖叫声。”

“我在阳台上向外看，看见了我所叙述的一切；我能感觉到热量，在我停留的整个期间——大约三分钟——那个人都在阳台上。他身材魁梧，中等身高，依我看，很年轻。我看得很清楚。我没看见有任何尸体被抬出庭院。我看不清阳台上那个人的面部特征，我以为他是中国人。当我第一次看见火灾时，阳台上没有人，他似乎是……

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 27, 1930

SUNDAY MORNING FIRE TRAGEDY

Sensational Testimony Given at U. S. Commissioner's
Inquiry: Medical Evidence Concerning Alleged
Injury to Mrs. Clausing's Skull

STRANGE STORY BY FELLOW LODGER

Question of Unconsciousness During Blaze Dealt with
by Medical Men Under Examination

Marked by new and sensational testimony offered by witnesses, plus conflicting evidence introduced by several spectators of the dramatic happenings and a surgeon's deposition of findings that visibly stirred an already tensed courtroom, the inquest on the body of Mrs. John G. Clausing who was burned beyond recognition in a fire at her home on Sunday morning was resumed at the American Court for China yesterday before Commissioner Alexander Krisel sitting as coroner and a jury composed of Messrs. Charles Raven, Gardner Crane, E. C. Stocker, John S. Potter, George Fitch and A. R. Hager. U. S. Attorney George Sellett conducted the case for the United States.

The first witness called at the morning session was M. M. Chapeaux, Commander of the Volunteer Fire Brigade of the French Concession who stated that a telephone message was received at the brigade headquarters at about 2.24 a.m. on the morning of the 24th inst. that a house at 146A. Route des Soeurs was on fire. Witness proceeded immediately with the first units under his command and found flames pouring from a third floor window. The unit immediately went to work and in about 15 to 20 minutes had the conflagration under such control that ladders were placed against the windows in the front of the house and Mr. Royere, Chief of the Fire Brigade ascended and entered the room. Special haste was made to get into the blazing structure as a youthful Russian had told him that a child had been left there by its parents.

The Body Discovered

On entering the room Mr. Royere found a body from which the legs were missing. He removed it to the verandah and soon after it was sent away in an ambulance to the French Mortuary. The witness could give little opinion on the origin of the fire as it was so intense as to obliterate all evidence.

Mr. Roygre then took the stand and corroborated the evidence of his predecessor. He stated that on entering the room he could not see because of the smoke, but groped around and struck against the bed on which by feeling as best he could he came upon the body which he immediately picked up and took outside. He noticed the legs were missing and went back for them. One was on the bed and the other lying some several feet away. Whether the body struck anything while he was removing it he could not answer, but it was possible that it had, as the passageway was extremely narrow, and the space which he traversed was very dark. The room was badly gutted and he did not feel capable of giving any opinion as to the fire's origin because there was little left on which to base an opinion. He expressed the belief that it could have been caused by a lighted match, cigarette, or any similar lighted object.

Charred Almost Beyond Recognition

Dr. K. W. Nance was next called and told of having examined the body on Monday at the mortuary and having found it so badly charred as to be almost beyond recognition. The only part untouched by the flames was the back and he believed this to be because the body was on its back during the fire. The hands were detached and the legs were severed about the knees. 在受询过程中，医务人员就火灾期间是否处于昏迷状态的问题进行了说明

昨日，美国驻华法院恢复了针对约翰·G·克劳辛（John G. Clausing）夫人遗体的死因调查。克劳辛夫人在周日清晨其住所发生的火灾中被烧得面目全非。此次调查由担任验尸官的美国驻华法院专员亚历山大·克里塞尔（Alexander Krisel）主持，陪审团成员包括查尔斯·雷文（Charles Raven）、加德纳·克兰（Gardner Crane）、E. C. 斯托克（E. C. Stocker）、约翰·S·波特（John S. Potter）、乔治·菲奇（George Fitch）和 A. R. 哈格（A. R. Hager）诸位先生。美国检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）代表美方主持此案。调查过程中，证人提供了新的且具轰动性的证词，几位目睹这一戏剧性事件的旁观者引入了相互矛盾的 evidence，以及一名外科医生提交的发现报告，这些都明显激起了本已紧张法庭的情绪。

上午庭审传唤的第一位证人是法租界志愿消防队队长 M. M. 沙波（M. M. Chapeaux）。他陈述称，当月24日凌晨约2点24分，消防队总部接到电话消息，称姐妹路（Route des Soeurs）146A号的一处房屋发生火灾。证人立即率领首批下属单位赶赴现场，发现火焰正从三楼窗户涌出。该单位立即投入工作，在约15至20分钟内将火势控制到足以将梯子架设在房屋正面窗户的程度，随后消防队队长罗耶尔（Royere）先生攀梯进入房间。之所以特别匆忙地进入燃烧的建筑，是因为一名年轻的俄罗斯人告诉他，有孩子被父母留在那里。

发现遗体

罗耶尔先生进入房间后，发现一具没有双腿的尸体。他将尸体移至阳台，不久后尸体由救护车送往法租界殡仪馆。由于火势猛烈，销毁了所有证据，证人对于火灾起因无法提供太多意见。

随后，罗伊格雷（Roygre）先生出庭作证，证实了其前任的证词。他陈述称，进入房间时因烟雾弥漫而无法视物，只能摸索前行，撞到了床上，通过尽可能仔细的触摸发现了尸体，他随即抱起尸体带至室外。他注意到双腿缺失，便返回寻找。一条腿在床上，另一条躺在几英尺外。至于在移出尸体过程中是否碰撞到任何物体，他无法回答，但有可能发生碰撞，因为通道极其狭窄，且他经过的空间非常黑暗。房间内部已被严重烧毁，他认为自己无法就火灾起因发表任何意见，因为几乎没有留下可供判断的依据。他表示相信火灾可能是由点燃的火柴、香烟或任何类似的燃烧物引起的。

几乎烧得面目全非
